newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EMI chief urges swift appointment of ECB board.
newsitem.headline: EMI chief urges swift appointment of ECB board.

text.p: The executive board of a European Central Bank should be decided as quickly as possible after a selection of the countries forming a single currency, Alexandre Lamfalussy, president of the European Monetary Institute, said.

Speaking to a monetary sub-committee of the European Parliament, Lamfalussy urged rapid selection of the governing board in order to allow the European Central Bank enough time for preparations in advance of the January 1, 1999 launch date for the euro.
"The executive board should be in place as quickly as possible after the choice of countries," Lamfalussy said. "Hopefully in the month of May (1998)."
The decision on which countries join a single currency will be made in late-April or early May of 1998.
The EMI has been concerned that the preparatory time between the selection of euro participants and the launch date may be too short for the ECB to become fully operational.
"Six months will be very short indeed. If it could be seven months or eight months, that would be much better," Lamfalussy added.
